text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"A cache must not use heuristics to determine freshness when an explicit expiration time is present.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [1] directly states this prohibition.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"A cache MUST NOT use heuristics to determine freshness when an explicit expiration time is present in the stored response."}]},{"claim_text":"A response with Cache-Control: max-age=600 is never given a heuristic lifetime.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"max-age is an explicit expiration mechanism, and heuristics are prohibited when an explicit expiration time is present.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"using either the Expires header field (Section 5.3) or the max-age response directive (Section 5.2.2.1)."},{"index":1,"quote":"A cache MUST NOT use heuristics to determine freshness when an explicit expiration time is present in the stored response."}]},{"claim_text":"If a response with max-age=600 also has s-maxage=60, a shared cache treats it as fresh for 60 seconds.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"s-maxage overrides max-age for a shared cache, so the shared cache uses 60 seconds as the maximum age.","citations":[{"index":7,"quote":"The s-maxage response directive indicates that, for a shared cache, the maximum age specified by this directive overrides the maximum age specified by either the max-age directive or the Expires header field."}]},{"claim_text":"A shared cache must ignore any Expires header when the response includes s-maxage.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [8] requires a shared cache recipient to ignore Expires when s-maxage is present.","citations":[{"index":8,"quote":"Likewise, if a response includes the s-maxage directive (Section 5.2.2.10), a shared cache recipient MUST ignore the Expires header field."}]},{"claim_text":"A client sending max-age=0 without max-stale is asking not to receive a stale response.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [3] says that without max-stale, the client does not wish to receive a stale response.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"The max-age request directive indicates that the client prefers a response whose age is less than or equal to the specified number of seconds. Unless the max-stale request directive is also present, the client does not wish to receive a stale response."}]},{"claim_text":"proxy-revalidate applies only to shared caches.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [6] specifies shared-cache behavior for proxy-revalidate and says it does not apply to private caches.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"This is analogous to must-revalidate (Section 5.2.2.2), except that proxy-revalidate does not apply to private caches."}]},{"claim_text":"A private cache holding a stale response marked proxy-revalidate may reuse it without revalidating.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"The general rule forbids generating a stale response unless the cache is disconnected or reuse is explicitly permitted; proxy-revalidate not applying to private caches does not by itself permit stale reuse.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"A cache MUST NOT generate a stale response unless it is disconnected or doing so is explicitly permitted by the client or origin server (e.g., by the max-stale request directive in Section 5.2.1, extension directives such as those defined in [RFC5861], or configuration in accordance with an out-of-band contract)."}]},{"claim_text":"must-revalidate binds every cache.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [5] says that in all circumstances a cache must not ignore the must-revalidate directive.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"In all circumstances, a cache MUST NOT ignore the must-revalidate directive"}]},{"claim_text":"A disconnected cache must return an error instead of the stale response when must-revalidate applies.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [5] requires a disconnected cache to generate an error response rather than reuse the stale response.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"if a cache is disconnected, the cache MUST generate an error response rather than reuse the stale response."}]},{"claim_text":"A client that sends max-stale=30 will accept a response up to 30 seconds past its freshness lifetime.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage [4] says a max-stale value makes the client willing to accept a response exceeded its freshness lifetime by no more than the specified number of seconds.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"If a value is present, then the client is willing to accept a response that has exceeded its freshness lifetime by no more than the specified number of seconds."}]},{"claim_text":"A client that sends max-stale=30 will not accept a response that is 45 seconds stale.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Because max-stale=30 permits exceeding freshness lifetime by no more than 30 seconds, 45 seconds exceeds the permitted amount.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"If a value is present, then the client is willing to accept a response that has exceeded its freshness lifetime by no more than the specified number of seconds."}]},{"claim_text":"If two suitable responses are stored, a cache uses the one with the earlier Date header.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage [9] requires using the most recent suitable response as determined by the Date header field, not the earlier one.","citations":[{"index":9,"quote":"When more than one suitable response is stored, a cache MUST use the most recent one (as determined by the Date header field)."}]}]}
